memoryText: And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me. Your throne shall be established forever.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 2 Samuel 7:16 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. This is the anchor verse for the whole unit. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse is the center of the unit. It is God’s promise to David, spoken through Nathan, and it is one of the most important sentences in the Old Testament.

“Your house.” David wanted to build God a house, and God promises to build his. This is a dynasty, a line of descendants who will sit on the throne. Every promise in the Bible after this moment hangs on this one thread: a son of David.

“And your kingdom.” It is not just a family that is promised, but a realm. The kingdom of David is the kingdom of God’s rule on earth, carried out through a human king.

“Shall be made sure forever before me.” The word “sure” means firm and established. The promise rests on God’s own faithfulness. David’s later sin would not cancel it. His descendants’ failures would not cancel it. God said it, and it stands.

“Your throne shall be established forever.” The repetition of “forever” is key. Every king in the line of David died. Solomon, in all his glory, fell into idolatry. The kingdom was divided, and the last king of Judah was taken to Babylon in chains. Yet the promise was never withdrawn. The prophets kept saying that a son of David would come, who would reign forever. Isaiah called him “the Prince of Peace.”

For the Christian, this verse is fulfilled in Jesus. “He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. And the Lord God will give to him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and of his kingdom there will be no end” (Luke 1:32-33). When you say this verse, you are saying that Jesus reigns. Memorize it. It is a promise that cannot fail.
weekInReview: This week brought David to the throne and to the center of God’s plan. You read the end of Saul at Gilboa and the lament of David over Saul and Jonathan. You saw David anointed over all Israel, take Jerusalem, and bring the ark up with dancing. You read the heart of the unit, the covenant of 2 Samuel 7, in which God promised David a house, a kingdom, and a throne forever. You saw David’s grace to Mephibosheth, and then the dark chapters of his sin with Bathsheba and his repentance. In the Psalms you prayed for the king in Psalm 20, gave thanks in Psalm 21, and heard the cry of Psalm 22, which Jesus prayed on the cross. Psalm 24 welcomed the King of glory, and Psalm 32 celebrated forgiveness. The week taught that God keeps his promises to David in spite of David’s sin, and that the true King would suffer and reign.
reflectionQuestions: God took David from the pasture and made him king, without any merit on David’s part. What has God done for you that you did not earn?
The covenant promised a son of David whose throne would last forever. How does Jesus fulfill this promise, and what does his reign mean for your life this week?
David hid his sin until Nathan confronted him, and then he confessed and was forgiven. Is there something you have been hiding? What would it look like to bring it into the light?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the promise to David and for Jesus, whose throne lasts forever.
Thank him for forgiveness that covers every sin.
Ask him to make you tender to his word.
